BRA.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Brazil broiler production ~14.9 Mt (#1 exporter, ~35% of global chicken trade), consumption ~10.2 Mt, exports ~5.3 Mt. ABPA reports record 2024 chicken exports near 5.3 Mt.

USA.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: US broiler production ~21.5 Mt (#1 producer), consumption ~17.9 Mt, exports ~3.3 Mt (leg quarters/dark meat to Mexico, Cuba, Angola, Asia).

CHN.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: China broiler production ~15.2 Mt, consumption ~16.1 Mt; net importer of chicken paws/wings/cuts (~0.75 Mt, mainly Brazil/US/Argentina).

POL.note: USDA/EU 2024: Poland is the EU's largest poultry producer (~3.2 Mt) and exporter (~1.7 Mt), shipping mainly intra-EU plus the UK.

THA.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Thailand broiler production ~3.45 Mt, exports ~1.15 Mt — a leading shipper of cooked/processed chicken to Japan, the EU and the UK.

NLD.note: Eurostat/USDA 2024: Netherlands is a poultry trade hub — production ~1.15 Mt but exports ~1.3 Mt on large re-exports (Rotterdam), with ~0.85 Mt imports.

TUR.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Turkey broiler production ~2.35 Mt, exports ~0.55 Mt to Iraq, the Gulf and Africa. Competitive halal supplier.

UKR.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Ukraine broiler production ~1.3 Mt (MHP-dominated), exports ~0.45 Mt mainly to the EU and the Gulf despite the war.

JPN.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Japan production ~1.7 Mt, consumption ~2.8 Mt; imports ~1.1 Mt (Brazil ~70%, Thailand cooked). One of the largest single-country chicken importers.

MEX.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Mexico broiler production ~4.0 Mt, consumption ~4.9 Mt; imports ~0.95 Mt (overwhelmingly US leg quarters). #1 destination for US chicken.

SAU.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Saudi production ~1.05 Mt, consumption ~1.75 Mt; imports ~0.7 Mt (mostly Brazilian halal). Largest Middle East chicken importer.

GBR.note: Defra/USDA 2024: UK production ~1.7 Mt, consumption ~2.35 Mt; net importer (~0.85 Mt) from the EU (Poland, Netherlands), Thailand and Brazil.

PHL.note: USDA PSD 2024/25: Philippines production ~1.45 Mt, consumption ~1.9 Mt; imports ~0.45 Mt (US, Brazil, EU), incl. mechanically deboned meat.

ZAF.note: USDA/SAPA 2024: South Africa production ~1.75 Mt, consumption ~2.15 Mt; imports ~0.45 Mt (Brazil bone-in, US/EU MDM), subject to anti-dumping duties. Largest sub-Saharan chicken importer.

ARE.note: USDA/Comtrade 2024: the UAE produces little chicken (~75 kt) but consumes ~0.6 Mt; imports ~0.65 Mt (Brazil halal dominant) and re-exports ~0.12 Mt across the Gulf.

IRQ.note: USDA PSD 2024/25 estimate: Iraq production ~0.45 Mt, consumption ~0.9 Mt, imports ~0.45 Mt (Brazil halal, Turkey, US). Iraq is a Comtrade non-reporter; balance on USDA, bilateral split modeled from partner-export data.

AGO.note: USDA/Comtrade-partner 2024: Angola produces ~35 kt and imports the bulk of consumption (~0.35 Mt, mainly US leg quarters and Brazil/EU). Partial Comtrade reporter; split modeled.

GHA.note: Comtrade/USDA 2024: Ghana produces ~75 kt but imports ~0.3 Mt of chicken (US, EU, Brazil), one of West Africa's largest import markets.

BEN.note: Comtrade 2024: Benin imports ~0.26 Mt of chicken far beyond domestic need and re-exports most informally into Nigeria (which bans poultry imports). A transit/re-export point.

CUB.note: USDA/US export data 2024: Cuba imports ~0.3 Mt of chicken, the bulk US leg quarters. Comtrade non-reporter; balance on USDA + US census export data, split modeled.

UN Comtrade 2024: Japan imported ~120 kt of chicken from the United States, mainly leg/thigh cuts.
UN Comtrade/USDA 2024: Mexico imported ~900 kt of chicken from the US (leg quarters, MDM) — the single largest US chicken export destination.
UN Comtrade/ABPA 2024: Saudi Arabia imported ~540 kt of (halal) chicken from Brazil, the dominant supplier to the largest Middle East market.
UN Comtrade 2024: France supplied ~60 kt of (halal) chicken to Saudi Arabia, a secondary supplier behind Brazil.
UN Comtrade/ABPA 2024: the UAE imported ~380 kt of (halal) chicken from Brazil, the leading supplier into the Gulf re-export hub.
UN Comtrade 2024 (China-reported): China imported ~480 kt of chicken (paws/wings/cuts) from Brazil, its largest poultry supplier.
UN Comtrade 2024: China imported ~120 kt of chicken from the US (chicken paws/feet a key high-value line).
UN Comtrade 2024: China imported ~60 kt of chicken from Argentina (paws/cuts).
UN Comtrade/SAPA 2024: South Africa imported ~230 kt of (bone-in) chicken from Brazil despite anti-dumping duties.
UN Comtrade 2024: South Africa imported ~80 kt of chicken from the US (leg quarters) under an AGOA-linked quota.
UN Comtrade 2024: the UK imported ~110 kt of chicken from Brazil, a significant non-EU supplier of frozen cuts.
UN Comtrade/Eurostat 2024: the UK imported ~220 kt of chicken from Poland, the largest single source post-Brexit.
UN Comtrade 2024: the UK imported ~130 kt of chicken from the Netherlands, partly Dutch re-exports.
UN Comtrade 2024: the UK imported ~90 kt of (mostly cooked) chicken from Thailand.
UN Comtrade/Eurostat 2024: Germany imported ~300 kt of chicken from Poland, the largest intra-EU poultry flow into Germany.
UN Comtrade/Eurostat 2024: Germany imported ~280 kt of chicken from the Netherlands.
UN Comtrade/Eurostat 2024: the Netherlands imported ~200 kt of chicken from Poland, feeding processing/re-export.
UN Comtrade/Eurostat 2024: France imported ~160 kt of chicken from Poland; France is a structural EU chicken net importer.
UN Comtrade/Eurostat 2024: France imported ~110 kt of chicken from Belgium (intra-EU border trade).
USDA/US Census export data 2024: Cuba imported ~280 kt of chicken from the US (leg quarters). Cuba is a Comtrade non-reporter; flow from US export records (mirror).
USDA/US export + partner-mirror 2024: Angola imported ~180 kt of chicken from the US (leg quarters). Partial Comtrade reporter; importer side modeled.
UN Comtrade partner-export 2024: Brazil shipped ~90 kt of chicken to Angola (mirror).
UN Comtrade partner-export 2024: Brazil shipped ~240 kt of (halal) chicken to Iraq. Iraq non-reporter; Brazil export side (mirror).
UN Comtrade partner-export 2024: Turkey shipped ~150 kt of chicken to neighbouring Iraq. Iraq non-reporter; Turkish export-side figure (mirror).
UN Comtrade 2024 (importer-reported): the Philippines imported ~130 kt of chicken from Brazil.
UN Comtrade/USDA 2024: the Philippines imported ~120 kt of chicken from the US, incl. mechanically deboned meat.
UN Comtrade 2024: Ghana imported ~90 kt of chicken from the US (leg quarters), a major West African import market.
UN Comtrade 2024: Ghana imported ~70 kt of chicken via the Netherlands (EU and re-export product).
UN Comtrade 2024: Ghana imported ~60 kt of chicken from Brazil.
UN Comtrade 2024: Benin imported ~90 kt of frozen chicken from the Netherlands, much onward (informal) into Nigeria.
UN Comtrade 2024: Benin imported ~70 kt of frozen chicken from Belgium, largely transit/re-export.
UN Comtrade 2024: Germany imported ~70 kt of (cooked) chicken from Thailand.
UN Comtrade/Eurostat 2024: the Netherlands imported ~110 kt of chicken from Ukraine (MHP), the EU absorbing most Ukrainian poultry exports.
UN Comtrade 2024: Mexico imported ~60 kt of chicken from Brazil, a secondary supplier behind the dominant US flow.
UN Comtrade 2024: Hong Kong imported ~110 kt of chicken from Brazil; a large per-capita importer and re-export gateway toward mainland China.

rankings.note: Exporter ranking in chicken-meat-equivalent kt from USDA PSD 2024/25 (Brazil + US ~50% of world chicken trade). Importer ranking from UN Comtrade 2024 importer-reported chicken imports plus USDA balances. WITS HTML was unavailable at build, so figures come from Comtrade/USDA published data.

companies.name: JBS
companies.metric: Group net revenue ~US$77bn (FY2024); Seara + Pilgrim's make it the world's largest poultry producer.
companies.note: World's largest protein company; Seara (Brazil) and Pilgrim's Pride (US/EU/Mexico) make it the top global chicken producer.
companies.improve: Should publish farm-level broiler traceability and feed-soy origin (Cerrado/Amazon deforestation link), plus country-by-country export volumes.

companies.name: Tyson Foods
companies.metric: Revenue ~US$53bn (FY2024); chicken segment ~US$17bn; largest US chicken processor.
companies.note: Largest US poultry processor; supplies US retail/foodservice and exports leg quarters/dark meat to Mexico, Asia, Africa.
companies.improve: Should disclose export volumes by destination and antibiotic-use/HPAI-biosecurity metrics per complex.

companies.name: BRF
companies.metric: Net revenue ~US$11bn (FY2024); Sadia/Perdigao; ~1.5 Mt poultry exports.
companies.note: One of the world's largest poultry exporters; leading halal chicken supplier to the Middle East via Sadia, with Turkey/Gulf processing.
companies.improve: Should publish destination-level halal export volumes and feed-soy traceability.

companies.name: Cargill
companies.metric: Group revenue ~US$160bn (FY2024); major poultry processor (US, Thailand, EU) and top poultry-feed supplier.
companies.note: Large integrated poultry processor (Sun Valley UK, Thai operations) and the dominant supplier of poultry feed and genetics.
companies.improve: Private; should report poultry output and feed-grain origination by country, plus deforestation-free soy sourcing.

companies.name: Pilgrim's Pride
companies.metric: Net revenue ~US$18bn (FY2024); #2 US chicken producer; large UK/EU and Mexico operations.
companies.note: Majority-owned by JBS; #2 US chicken producer and a major European (Moy Park) and Mexican supplier.
companies.improve: Should publish export and intra-group transfer volumes and clarify how much rolls into JBS group concentration.

companies.name: Wens Foodstuffs
companies.metric: Revenue ~US$14bn (FY2024); one of China's largest broiler and hog producers.
companies.note: Leading Chinese integrated poultry (and pork) producer, central to domestic broiler supply; production mostly for the home market.
companies.improve: Should disclose feed-import (soy/corn) dependence by source country and HPAI metrics.

global.note: World broiler/chicken meat, kt, USDA PSD. Chicken is the world's most-produced and fastest-growing meat; output passed ~105 Mt and chicken trade ~13.8 Mt in 2024. Total poultry (incl. turkey/duck) is larger; series here is the broiler/chicken basis for HS 0207.

forecast.method: OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook envelope; 2030=2024×(1+rate)^6. Global chicken demand projected to rise ~1.5-2.5%/yr, the fastest of any major meat, led by Asia, Africa and the Middle East.
